prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1461; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe during a lane change and said the other vehicle drifted into their lane as they were merging. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been cooperative in providing details.

Entry 2: Reviewed photos of both vehicles, which show damage consistent with the described impact. The other driver's statement matches the claimant's account, and two independent witnesses also describe the collision as reported.

Entry 3: Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash following the impact. Claimant was not entirely certain of their exact seating position at the moment of contact, which I have noted for the file. The injury pattern appears consistent with the force of the crash.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy. Searched prior claim history and found no earlier injury to the neck or upper back. The vehicle's repair history also shows no prior damage to the affected panels.

Entry 5: A neighbor mentioned seeing the car with body damage several weeks before the claimed accident date. I will follow up by requesting additional information, though this has not yet been verified against other sources.

Entry 6: Claimant has repeated the same account in each conversation with no material differences. Treatment has followed a typical course and symptoms have steadily improved, with care tapering as recovery progressed.
